mini.es: Completa con although, despite, however, whereas o so that.
mini.en: Complete with although, despite, however, whereas or so that.

___ the traffic, we arrived on time.
It's cheap. ___, it isn't very good.

explain.es: Los conectores (linkers) unen ideas y dicen qué relación hay entre ellas: contraste (aunque, a pesar de, sin embargo), comparación (mientras que), resultado (por lo tanto) y finalidad (para, para que). La clave en inglés es lo que va detrás: una frase completa, un nombre, un -ing o un infinitivo. Usarlos bien sube la nota de Organisation en el Writing del B2 First.
explain.en: Linkers connect ideas and show the relationship between them: contrast, comparison, result and purpose. The key is what comes after them.

explain.title: 1 · ALTHOUGH, THOUGH, EVEN THOUGH
explain.es: Significan aunque. Detrás va una frase completa (sujeto + verbo). Pueden ir al principio (con coma entre las dos partes) o en medio. even though es más enfático (aun cuando); though es más informal y también puede ir al final = eso sí, de todas formas. ¡No añadas but en la otra parte!
explain.en: They mean aunque and are followed by a clause (subject + verb). Even though is more emphatic; though can also go at the end. Don't add but.

examples.en: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
examples.es: Aunque llovía, salimos a dar un paseo.

examples.en: She went to work even though she had a temperature.
examples.es: Fue a trabajar aunque tenía fiebre.

examples.en: The food was great. The service was slow, though.
examples.es: La comida estaba buenísima. Eso sí, el servicio era lento.

explain.title: Truco: ¿frase o nombre?
explain.es: Antes de elegir, mira lo que viene detrás. ¿Hay sujeto + verbo (it was raining)? → although / even though. ¿Hay un nombre o -ing (the rain, being tired)? → despite / in spite of. En español: aunque + verbo conjugado = although; a pesar de + nombre / infinitivo = despite. Y para + infinitivo = to; para que + subjuntivo = so that.
explain.en: Subject + verb → although. Noun / -ing → despite. Para = to; para que = so that.

explain.title: 2 · DESPITE, IN SPITE OF
explain.es: Significan a pesar de. Detrás va un nombre, un pronombre o un verbo en -ing, nunca sujeto + verbo. Para meter una frase completa usa despite the fact that (= a pesar de que). ¡Ojo! despite no lleva of; in spite sí: despite of.
explain.en: They mean a pesar de and are followed by a noun or -ing. With a clause, use despite the fact that. Never despite of.

examples.en: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
examples.es: A pesar del tráfico, llegamos a tiempo.

examples.en: In spite of being tired, he finished the report.
examples.es: A pesar de estar cansado, terminó el informe.

examples.en: Despite the fact that she's only 22, she runs her own company.
examples.es: A pesar de que solo tiene 22 años, dirige su propia empresa.

explain.title: ¿ALTHOUGH o DESPITE?
explain.es: Significan casi lo mismo, pero detrás llevan cosas distintas. Mira lo que viene después: ¿hay sujeto + verbo? → although. ¿Hay un nombre o -ing? → despite.
explain.en: Subject + verb → although. Noun or -ing → despite.

explain.title: 3 · HOWEVER, NEVERTHELESS
explain.es: However = sin embargo. Une dos oraciones separadas: va al principio de la segunda, después de un punto (o punto y coma) y seguido de coma. ¡No puede unir dos frases solo con una coma, como but! Nevertheless es igual pero más formal. También puede ir en medio, entre comas: The plan, however, failed.
explain.en: However links two separate sentences: full stop (or semicolon) + However + comma. Nevertheless is more formal.

examples.en: The flat is small. However, it's very central.
examples.es: El piso es pequeño. Sin embargo, está muy céntrico.

examples.en: We tried to book a table; however, the restaurant was full.
examples.es: Intentamos reservar mesa; sin embargo, el restaurante estaba lleno.

examples.en: The results were good. Nevertheless, there is still work to do.
examples.es: Los resultados fueron buenos. No obstante, aún queda trabajo por hacer.

explain.title: 4 · WHEREAS, WHILE
explain.es: Sirven para comparar dos cosas opuestas: mientras que. Detrás va una frase completa. Suelen ir en medio (con coma delante) o al principio. while es más frecuente al hablar; whereas suena más formal. Ojo: while también significa mientras (tiempo): I read while I wait.
explain.en: They compare two opposite facts (mientras que). While is more common in speech; whereas is more formal.

examples.en: I'm an early bird, whereas my partner hates mornings.
examples.es: Yo soy madrugador, mientras que mi pareja odia las mañanas.

examples.en: While some people love social media, others find it stressful.
examples.es: Mientras que a algunos les encantan las redes sociales, a otros les estresan.

examples.en: In Spain we have lunch at two, whereas in the UK people eat at around one.
examples.es: En España comemos a las dos, mientras que en el Reino Unido se come sobre la una.

explain.title: 5 · THEREFORE: resultado
explain.es: Therefore = por lo tanto, por consiguiente. Introduce un resultado o una conclusión. Es más formal que so: ideal para redacciones e informes. Va al principio de la segunda oración (tras punto o punto y coma, con coma) o antes del verbo principal: It is therefore important to…
explain.en: Therefore introduces a result or conclusion. It is more formal than so.

examples.en: The train was cancelled. Therefore, we had to take a taxi.
examples.es: Cancelaron el tren. Por lo tanto, tuvimos que coger un taxi.

examples.en: Prices have risen; therefore, many families are spending less.
examples.es: Los precios han subido; por lo tanto, muchas familias gastan menos.

examples.en: It is therefore essential to book in advance.
examples.es: Por lo tanto, es imprescindible reservar con antelación.

items.es: ¿Empiezas una oración nueva? → However, / Therefore, (punto antes, coma después).
Finalidad: mismo sujeto → (in order) to + infinitivo. Otro sujeto → so that + can / could.
items.en: Same subject → to. Different subject → so that.

items.es: Revisa la puntuación y el registro (formal en redacciones).

explain.title: 6 · Finalidad: IN ORDER TO, SO THAT
explain.title_en: Purpose: in order to, so that
explain.es: Para decir para qué hacemos algo: to / in order to / so as to + infinitivo (para + infinitivo). Negativa: in order not to / so as not to. Si hay otro sujeto o un modal: so that + sujeto + can / could / will / would (para que + subjuntivo). ¡Nunca for to ni for + infinitivo!
explain.en: Purpose: (in order) to / so as to + infinitive. With another subject or a modal: so that + subject + can / could / will / would. Never for to.
formula: *(in order) to / so as to* + infinitivo
*so that* + sujeto + can / could / will / would

examples.en: I'm saving money in order to buy a car.
examples.es: Estoy ahorrando para comprarme un coche.

examples.en: We left early so as not to miss the train.
examples.es: Salimos pronto para no perder el tren.

examples.en: I'll send you the address so that you can find the place.
examples.es: Te mando la dirección para que encuentres el sitio.

items.en: Although I'd studied a lot, I found the exam really hard.
items.es: Aunque había estudiado mucho, el examen me pareció dificilísimo.

items.en: Despite the bad reviews, the film was a huge success.
items.es: A pesar de las malas críticas, la película fue un exitazo.

items.en: The job is well paid. However, the hours are very long.
items.es: El trabajo está bien pagado. Sin embargo, el horario es larguísimo.

items.en: My brother loves football, whereas I can't stand it.
items.es: A mi hermano le encanta el fútbol, mientras que yo no lo soporto.

items.en: The company lost money last year; therefore, it had to cut jobs.
items.es: La empresa perdió dinero el año pasado; por lo tanto, tuvo que recortar plantilla.

items.en: I set two alarms so that I wouldn't oversleep.
items.es: Puse dos alarmas para no quedarme dormido.

items.en: In spite of having a cold, she ran the marathon.
items.es: A pesar de estar resfriada, corrió el maratón.

items.en: We took the motorway in order to save time.
items.es: Cogimos la autopista para ahorrar tiempo.

items.en: Even though he's lived in London for ten years, he still hates the weather.
items.es: Aunque lleva diez años viviendo en Londres, sigue odiando el clima.

items.en: While cities offer more jobs, villages offer a calmer lifestyle.
items.es: Mientras que las ciudades ofrecen más trabajo, los pueblos ofrecen una vida más tranquila.

items.en: I turned my phone off so as not to be disturbed.
items.es: Apagué el móvil para que no me molestaran.

items.en: Nice hotel. A bit noisy, though.
items.es: Buen hotel. Eso sí, algo ruidoso.

explain.note: Registro: en emails y al hablar → but, so, to, though. En redacciones e informes → however, therefore, in order to, whereas, although.
explain.note_en: Informal: but, so, to. Formal writing: however, therefore, in order to, whereas.

items.bad: Despite it was raining, we played.
items.good: Although it was raining, we played. / Despite the rain, we played.
items.why: despite + nombre / -ing; con sujeto + verbo → although.

items.bad: Despite of the price, I bought it.
items.why: despite nunca lleva of (in spite of sí).

items.bad: Although I was tired, but I went out.
items.good: Although I was tired, I went out.
items.why: Con although no se añade but: una sola conjunción.
items.why_en: Don't use although and but together.

items.bad: The hotel was cheap, however it was dirty.
items.good: The hotel was cheap. However, it was dirty.
items.why: however no une frases con coma: punto (o ;) + However,

items.bad: I'm learning English for get a better job.
items.good: I'm learning English to get a better job.
items.why: «para + infinitivo» = to / in order to, nunca for.

items.bad: I left early for not to miss the bus.
items.good: I left early so as not to miss the bus.
items.why: Finalidad negativa: so as not to / in order not to.
items.why_en: Negative purpose: so as not to.

items.bad: Even I was ill, I went to work.
items.good: Even though I was ill, I went to work.

items.bad: In spite of be tired, he won.
items.good: In spite of being tired, he won.
items.why: Tras despite / in spite of → verbo en -ing.

lines.en: So, what did you think of the flat in Malasaña?
lines.es: Bueno, ¿qué te pareció el piso de Malasaña?

lines.en: I liked it. Although it's quite small, it's really bright.
lines.es: Me gustó. Aunque es bastante pequeño, tiene muchísima luz.

lines.en: True. However, the rent is a bit high for us.
lines.es: Es verdad. Sin embargo, el alquiler es algo alto para nosotros.

lines.en: The other one is cheaper, whereas this one is much more central.
lines.es: El otro es más barato, mientras que este es mucho más céntrico.

lines.en: Despite the price, I think it's worth it. We'd save on transport.
lines.es: A pesar del precio, creo que merece la pena. Ahorraríamos en transporte.

lines.en: Good point. Let's call the agent today so that nobody else gets it first.
lines.es: Buena idea. Llamemos hoy a la agencia para que no nos lo quite nadie.

lines.en: OK. I'll ask for a discount in order to keep the rent under 1,000 euros.
lines.es: Vale. Pediré un descuento para mantener el alquiler por debajo de 1.000 euros.

lines.en: Perfect. We're signing for two years, though, so let's read the contract carefully.
lines.es: Perfecto. Eso sí, firmamos por dos años, así que leamos bien el contrato.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta

exercises.text_title: Is working from home here to stay?
text: Since the pandemic, millions of people have started working from home. Although many workers love the freedom it gives them, others feel lonely and isolated. So, is it really a good idea?

On the one hand, remote workers save time and money because they don't have to commute. My cousin Marta, for example, works from home in order to spend more time with her children. Despite having a smaller salary than before, she says she is much happier.

On the other hand, working from home is not for everyone. In an office, young employees learn by watching experienced colleagues, whereas at home they have nobody to ask. In my view, a mix of office and home working is the best option. Therefore, I believe companies should let their employees choose.

items.q: All workers enjoy working from home.
items.why: Although many love it, others feel lonely and isolated.

items.q: Marta earns more money now than before.
items.why: Despite having a smaller salary than before…

items.q: The writer thinks a mix of office and home working is best.
Why does Marta work from home?
items.a: In order to spend more time with her children.

items.q: What problem do young employees have at home?
items.a: They have nobody to ask (they can't learn by watching experienced colleagues).

items.q: Find a linker that introduces a purpose.
Find a linker that compares two opposite situations.
Rewrite with although: 'Despite having a smaller salary, she is much happier.'
items.a: Although she has a smaller salary, she is much happier.
